title: High Level UKPNP Delegation Led by Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri Meets Baroness Emma Nicholson in London
excerpt: UKPNP delegation holds high level political briefing in London with Baroness Emma Nicholson on Kashmir developments and international follow up.
author: Special Correspondent, London UK

heroImage.caption: UKPNP delegation meets Baroness Emma Nicholson in London.

body.text: A high level delegation of the United Kashmir People’s National Party, UKPNP, led by its Exiled Chairman Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri, held a formal meeting and briefing with Baroness Emma Nicholson.
Baroness Nicholson served as Member of the European Parliament and Rapporteur on Kashmir. Her 2007 report remains one of the most important documents on the issue.
The meeting focused on political conditions in all regions of the historical State of Jammu and Kashmir, human rights challenges, and possible steps for international follow up.
The delegation included Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan and senior UKPNP leadership from Europe and the UK.
Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri thanked Baroness Nicholson for her long-standing engagement and leadership on Kashmir.
The delegation compared the findings of the 2007 report with current developments, including changes in Indian and Pakistani administered regions.
They reaffirmed that Jammu, Kashmir, Ladakh, Gilgit Baltistan, and Azad Jammu and Kashmir form one historical and political entity.
The delegation highlighted decades of division, displacement, and restrictions on civic rights.
Baroness Nicholson stressed the need for Kashmiri youth in the diaspora to be well integrated, educated, and active in politics.
The delegation explained how misinformation and distorted history have affected communities in Azad Kashmir, Gilgit Baltistan, and the diaspora.
They noted that pro‑peace and pro‑Kashmir parties face discrimination, while extremist groups operate freely.
The delegation described recent protests, blackouts, and human rights violations in Azad Kashmir.
They underlined that Azad Kashmir and Gilgit Baltistan have no representation in Pakistan’s National Assembly or Senate.
